page: Amazon Web Services x8i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor is supported by a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps, and includes no local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2174.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 2128.19, both placing in the top 25%. Text processing is a notable highlight, scoring 2981.0 on Geekbench to reach the top 10% tier. For language processing, the server achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 372.71 tokens per second using a small 135M LLM model, though medium 7B model generation drops to an average 15.28 tokens per second. Multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally sit in the average range, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 13193.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 127.98 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the x8i.4xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of local storage means all storage operations must run over the network, which is limited to an 8 Gbps baseline. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including in-memory databases like Redis, large-scale text processing pipelines, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
